title: What each format can represent

marks.linked: held as an external community-standard file (not copied) and queried through the shared index
marks.convention: representable by convention: stored and read back through the public API in a general-purpose slot, structure lost or ad hoc

rules: the evidence decides; only a genuinely ambiguous cell gives the other tool the better mark, and its note starts with 'Judgement call'

AnnData / MuData (and SpatialData table) elements rated in their most favourable orientation (spots, cells or loci as observations); these orientations exclude each other in one object (one AnnData, one MuData modality)
a test that needed a generic slot backs at most 'by convention', an external file 'linked'

a data table serialised to JSON text in a descriptive metadata attribute does not count (recorded with counted: false); provenance metadata there does, and so do scalar key-values describing the object that carries the attribute (each cell's own cooler in a .scool)

partial reads: native = one cell's / chromosome's rows are read from disk without reading the other rows (beyond the selection key column); by convention = only by scanning every row (streamed) or with part of the data loaded whole

by convention needs a normal use of the format that just lacks the structure; an encoding that merely writes (e.g. tracing traces as per-trace column sets of cooler bins tables, an embedding as one metadata key per dimension) is rated not supported, with the test still reported

col_defs.coords: the x, y, z position of every spot (one imaged or reconstructed locus in one trace), with its unit.
col_defs.hierarchy: which trace and which cell each spot belongs to, as nested levels rather than loose labels.
col_defs.spot_signals: values measured per spot, such as immunofluorescence intensity or z-scores at that spot.
col_defs.bin_signals: values per genomic bin shared by all cells, such as bulk ATAC / ChIP tracks or GC content.
col_defs.cells: a table of scalar properties per cell, such as cell type, volume or RNA counts.
col_defs.cell_emb: a multi-dimensional vector per cell, such as a PCA, UMAP or learned embedding.
col_defs.cell_pos: where each cell is in the tissue or field of view (centroid and / or outline), with unit and coordinate frame.
col_defs.contacts: locus × locus contact counts (Hi-C-type maps), in bulk or per cell.
col_defs.intervals: genomic intervals and interval pairs called on the data, such as TADs and loops.
col_defs.points: 3-D points that are not genomic loci, such as RNA spots or protein puncta.
col_defs.provenance: analysis results stored as data together with the function, parameters and version that produced them.
col_defs.partial: reading one cell's or one chromosome's rows from disk without reading the rest of the data.

bin_signals.note: none of the 12 tables is indexed by genomic locus; a per-locus value can only be repeated on every spot as an optional column

contacts.note: no contact-matrix table in the 12 FOF-CT tables

provenance.note: header #Software_* fields describe the tools that produced a table; analysis results only as optional columns

partial.note: plain CSV without an index: one cell or chromosome is found only by scanning every row (streamed, e.g. pandas chunksize, so memory stays bounded)

coords.note: obsm['spatial'] (n_obs, 3), a community convention; no trace / unit structure

hierarchy.note: one obs axis: cell_id / trace_id only as obs columns; spots and cells cannot both be observations

spot_signals.note: spots as obs: X / layers / obs columns. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

bin_signals.note: loci as var (cells × loci, as for scATAC peaks): var table. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

cells.note: cells as obs: obs table. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).

cell_emb.note: cells as obs: obsm (X_umap, X_pca), the slot designed for per-observation multi-dimensional annotations. Rated in the most favourable orientation; one AnnData has a single obs axis, so spots, cells and loci cannot all be first-class in the same object (see the hierarchy column).
